passage:
Sam opened his lunch box and found only rice. The chicken, egg, and vegetables were gone.
He looked at Ben, who sat next to him. Ben was eating chicken, egg, and vegetables, but he also looked surprised.
"This is not my lunch," Ben said. "My box had noodles."
They checked their bags. Both lunch boxes were blue, and both had no names on them. After asking around, they found a third blue box in Lily's bag. Lily had eaten noodles and thought her mother had changed the menu.
The three students laughed, but Sam was still hungry. Ben gave him half of the chicken, and Lily shared some fruit.
The next day, all three lunch boxes had large name stickers on them. Their teacher said it was a simple lesson: when things look the same on the outside, names can save lunch.
